A support must be an acyclic directed graph without duplicate edges. Unlisted explicit edge weights are 0. A support route uses support: through_b; a Pinned DAG model can declare allocation: equal or weighted, with weight_basis: capacity or explicit as applicable and edge_weights naming the explicit vector. Named Pinned DAGs refuse residual_snapshot. Path-only routes do not accept DAG split controls.

Other routing models use type: shortest_paths, distributed_te or centralized_te. For example:

model:
  admission: lossless
  routing:
    type: shortest_paths
    allocation: weighted
    weight_basis: capacity
    tie_break: fewer_hops
    multipath: true
    parallel_edges: true
routing.type Keys shortest_paths allocation (equal by default, weighted or optimized), source_allocation (equal or optimized), weight_basis (capacity, explicit or residual_snapshot), edge_weights (a name in weights), tie_break, multipath, parallel_edges distributed_te tunnel_count: {per_head: N} (required), min_unreserved_bandwidth (a physical amount), cost_ceiling, tie_break, parallel_edges centralized_te source_allocation (optimized or equal, required), tunnel_count: {per_head: N} with optional up_to: true, prefer_headroom pinned routes, and for a DAG allocation, weight_basis and edge_weights (above)

admission is lossless (the default) or lossy. cost_ceiling is {type: absolute, value: C} or {type: stretch, value: "3/2"}; stretch values are exact: integers, fraction strings ("3/2") or decimal strings ("1.16"), never rounded to a binary64 value, and the ceiling is inclusive. A key the routing type does not have, or a per_head outside 1 to 10000, is refused at load; preparation refuses combinations the engine does not accept, such as weight_basis without allocation: weighted. What each model does: Routing models and admission and Tunnels and TE ingress pools.

docs.title: Routing domains and the WCMP controller
docs.text:
A WCMP controller programs every SHORTEST_PATHS_WCMP demand toward one BGP-edge router with one destination-wide weight table per demand set and destination:

routing:
  igp_domain: {path: '^(A|B)[12]$'}
  bgp_edge: {path: '^DC_'}
wcmp_controller: {scope: group}      # next_hop (default) | group | all_routers
forwarding_groups:
  ingress:
    router: DC_A
    groups:
      - children: [{edge: {link: 'DC_A|A1|0', direction: forward}}]
      - share: "1/2"
        children: [{edge: {link: 'DC_A|A2|0', direction: forward}}]

Both populations are required, nonempty and disjoint (selected like demand endpoints, so disabled nodes are outside them). A programmed demand has one destination, in bgp_edge, and its sources lie in either population. wcmp_controller.scope is next_hop (the default), group or all_routers. The routes the controller uses and what each scope programs: Routing domains and the WCMP controller and Forwarding groups and their caps.

Under group, every programmed router needs a tree whose leaves are exactly its members toward t, and every declared tree must be used, so a tree at a router the controller never programs is refused, while a source with no route (an empty DAG) is not programmed and needs none; under next_hop and all_routers trees are validated and unused. Shares are exact: an integer, a "p/q" or decimal string (YAML floats are refused); a positive share whose children all have share 0 is refused.

Placement and maximum supported demand (MSD) results report the tables under controller; a router not listed there splits by ECMP. These are the tables of the network without failures; in a failure case the converged state computes its own tables, which are not exported (Failures: patterns, cases and states).

docs.title: Weight approximation
docs.text: Weights whose exact reduced integers reach 2^62 are apportioned over 2^62 - 1 (one unit for each positive member, then highest averages, earlier member on ties) and reported in units_report.weight_approximations with the exact largest relative error: one entry per router (controller.<set>.<t>.router.<r>) and, under all_routers, one per source vector, naming the source with the largest error (controller.<set>.<t>.source.<s>). Source weights are the volumes' exact binary values reduced to integers, so volumes 1000 and 0.1 (whose binary value has a 2^55 denominator) are apportioned and reported, while 1000000 and 1 stay exact.

docs.title: Selector Fields
docs.text:
The source and target fields accept either:

  • A string regex pattern matched against node names
  • A selector object with path, group_by, and/or match fields

Selecting nodes describes both.

docs.title: Traffic Modes (mode)
docs.text:
Controls how source and target node sets are paired:

  • combine: One source-set/destination-set demand, with one ordered roster of sources (Demands: how traffic enters).
  • pairwise: Create one demand for each distinct selected source/target node pair. Node-to-itself pairs receive no share.

A matrix whose sources and targets share nodes, such as all pairs of four sites, needs each shared node in a group of its own on both sides, for example by capturing each name (^(A|B|C|D)$) or with group_by: name. The declared volume is split over the pairs:

network:
  nodes: {A: {}, B: {}, C: {}, D: {}}
  links:
    - {source: A, target: B, capacity: 10}
    - {source: B, target: C, capacity: 10}
    - {source: C, target: D, capacity: 10}
    - {source: D, target: A, capacity: 10}
demands:
  matrix:
    # 12 ordered pairs of distinct sites, 48 / 12 = 4 each
    - {source: "^(A|B|C|D)$", target: "^(A|B|C|D)$", volume: 48, mode: pairwise}
workflow:
  - {type: TrafficMatrixPlacement, name: matrix, demand_set: matrix}

A pattern without a capturing group makes one group of all its nodes, so the same matrix written source: "^[ABCD]$", target: "^[ABCD]$" is refused:

network:
  nodes: {A: {}, B: {}, C: {}, D: {}}
demands:
  matrix:
    - {source: "^[ABCD]$", target: "^[ABCD]$", volume: 48, mode: pairwise}
workflow:
  - {type: TrafficMatrixPlacement, name: matrix, demand_set: matrix}

Overlapping source and target groups are refused in demands, capacity and path questions (no target is silently dropped), except a pair that is one and the same node: a demand gives it no share, and capacity and path questions give it a zero-valued self row. A declaration whose every pair is a node-to-itself pair or a same-label group pair is reported whole as discarded, with its reason. If a declaration is excluded for both reasons, the first exclusion in canonical group and node order supplies its reason. A selection that matches no active node keeps its share as an empty_selection discard; a group whose nodes are all filtered out is not selected and takes no share (Demands: how traffic enters).

docs.title: Group Modes (group_mode)
docs.text:
When using group_by selectors, controls how grouped nodes produce demands:

  • flatten (default): Flatten all groups into a single source/target set, then apply mode
  • per_group: Create one branch per source group with combined targets, or pairwise node branches within labels shared by both selectors. Branches whose only pairs are node-to-itself pairs receive no share; non-diagonal overlap refuses, and an empty branch keeps its discarded share.
  • group_pairwise: Split across ordered source/target group pairs with distinct labels; identical labels receive no share. Apply the selected node mode within each remaining group pair

Example with group_mode:

demands:
  inter_dc_traffic:
    # Each DC pair gets its own demand
    - source:
        group_by: "dc"
      target:
        group_by: "dc"
      volume: 1000
      mode: "combine"
      group_mode: "group_pairwise"    # Creates dc1->dc2, dc2->dc1, dc1->dc3, etc.
mode group_mode Result combine flatten Single aggregated demand across all nodes combine per_group One demand per source group (targets combined) combine group_pairwise One demand per (source_group, target_group) pair with distinct labels pairwise flatten Individual demands for distinct node pairs pairwise per_group Distinct node pairs within each shared label pairwise group_pairwise Distinct node pairs within each distinct-label group pair

Each declared physical total is converted to units once, then split over its eligible pairs by integer quotient and remainder; declared units equal resolved plus discarded units (Demands: how traffic enters).

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Demands that omit both preset and model use SHORTEST_PATHS_ECMP. A MaxFlow step that omits both asks unrestricted optimized lossless maximum flow (TE_MAXFLOW_UNLIM), in YAML and Python. Each preset is one explicit model:

Preset model equivalent Question SHORTEST_PATHS_ECMP {routing: {type: shortest_paths}, admission: lossless} IP/IGP routing with equal splits among equal-cost next hops at each router; what does not fit is not admitted, and a filled next hop can block later demands assigned to it SHORTEST_PATHS_ECMP_LOSSY {routing: {type: shortest_paths}, admission: lossy} The same routing with best-effort forwarding: traffic is sent and lost at sources and on edges SHORTEST_PATHS_WCMP {routing: {type: shortest_paths, allocation: weighted, weight_basis: capacity}} Capacity-weighted static shortest-path routing with lossless equal source allocation; with a wcmp_controller, the controller's table instead (a MaxFlow step then refuses this preset) SHORTEST_PATHS_MAXFLOW {routing: {type: shortest_paths, allocation: optimized, source_allocation: optimized}} Optimized capacity on the union of the selected shortest-path supports TE_MAXFLOW_UNLIM {routing: {type: centralized_te, source_allocation: optimized}} Unrestricted optimized lossless traffic engineering TE_ECMP_16_LSP {routing: {type: centralized_te, source_allocation: optimized, tunnel_count: {per_head: 16}, prefer_headroom: true}} Controller tunnels (T2), exactly 16 per head TE_ECMP_UP_TO_256_LSP {routing: {type: centralized_te, source_allocation: optimized, tunnel_count: {per_head: 256, up_to: true}, prefer_headroom: true}} Controller tunnels (T2), up to 256 per head

What each model does: Routing models and admission; tunnel counts: Tunnels and TE ingress pools.

docs.title: failures - Failure Policies
docs.text:
Named failure policies:

failures:
  single_link_failure:
    modes:                       # Weighted modes; each draw picks exactly one
      - weight: 1.0
        rules:
          - scope: "link"
            mode: "choice"
            count: 1

  weighted_modes:                # Example of weighted multi-mode policy
    modes:
      - weight: 0.30
        rules:
          - scope: "risk_group"
            mode: "choice"
            count: 1
            weight_by: distance_km

      - weight: 0.35
        rules:
          - scope: "link"
            mode: "choice"
            count: 3
            match:                       # Attribute conditions inside match block
              logic: "and"
              conditions:
                - attr: "link_type"
                  op: "=="
                  value: "dc_to_pop"
            weight_by: target_capacity

      - weight: 0.25
        rules:
          - scope: "node"
            path: "^dc[1-3]/.*"          # Path filter (regex)
            mode: "choice"
            count: 1
            match:
              logic: "and"
              conditions:
                - attr: "node_type"
                  op: "!="
                  value: "dc_region"
            weight_by: attached_capacity_gbps

      - weight: 0.10
        rules:
          - scope: "link"
            mode: "choice"
            count: 4
            match:
              logic: "or"                # Any condition matches
              conditions:
                - attr: "link_type"
                  op: "=="
                  value: "leaf_spine"
                - attr: "link_type"
                  op: "=="
                  value: "intra_group"
                - attr: "link_type"
                  op: "=="
                  value: "inter_group"

docs.title: Policy-Level Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description modes array required List of weighted failure modes attrs object {} Policy metadata (e.g., description) expand_groups boolean false Also fail every node and link that shares a risk group with a failed one, whether a node, link or risk-group rule failed it (the members of a failed risk group fail with or without this flag)

A failed risk group always cascades to its child groups recursively.

Each entry of modes accepts weight (required, non-negative), rules (required) and optional attrs; mode attrs are recorded as mode_attrs in failure traces.

Risk group expansion example:

failures:
  srlg_failures:
    expand_groups: true      # Spread failures across shared risk-group memberships
    attrs:
      description: "Shared-risk link group failure simulation"
    modes:
      - weight: 1.0
        rules:
          - scope: "risk_group"
            mode: "choice"
            count: 1

docs.title: Selection Modes
docs.text:
• all: Select all matching entities
  • choice: Select specific count of entities (optionally weighted)
  • random: Select each entity independently with given probability

docs.title: Rule Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description scope string Entity type: node, link, or risk_group (required) mode string Selection mode: all, choice, or random (default: all) count integer Number of entities to select (for choice mode), at least 1 probability number Selection probability 0-1 (for random mode) path string Regex filter on entity name (links match against their source\|target form) match object Attribute conditions block with logic and conditions weight_by string Attribute name for weighted sampling in choice mode

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Each mode has a non-negative weight. Each draw picks one mode with probability proportional to the weights, applies all its rules and fails the union of their selections.
  • At least one mode must have weight > 0; a policy whose modes all have zero weight is refused where the policy is built, in Python and YAML. Modes with zero weight are never selected.
  • Condition syntax uses the same operators as link/demand selectors. See Conditions for the full reference.

docs.title: workflow - Analysis Steps
docs.text:
The ordered list of analysis steps:

workflow:
  - type: NetworkStats
    name: network_statistics
  - type: MaximumSupportedDemand
    name: msd_baseline
    demand_set: baseline_traffic_matrix
  - type: TrafficMatrixPlacement
    name: tm_placement
    demand_set: baseline_traffic_matrix
    failure_policy: weighted_modes
    iterations: 1000

Built-in steps:

  • BuildGraph: Export graph to JSON (node-link) for external analysis
  • NetworkStats: Node, link, capacity and degree statistics
  • MaxFlow: Capacity between node sets, optionally under failure draws
  • TrafficMatrixPlacement: Placement of a named demand set, optionally under failure draws
  • MaximumSupportedDemand: Search for the largest tested feasible alpha (the demand multiplier) for a named demand set (Maximum supported demand)
  • CostPower: Aggregate capex and power by network hierarchy level
  • TunnelCountAnalysis: Rows per tunnel count for the tunnelled TE demands of a named demand set

See Workflow Steps for detailed configuration.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Every JSON object of a results file (ngraph/schemas/results.json) and what each field means, generated from the result declarations. How NetGraph computes explains the numbers. They come in five kinds:

  • Bandwidth units: every *_units field and the native amounts, integers in units of the run's resolution q (the units report holds q); units × q is the physical amount.
  • Physical amounts: inputs, question offers and designs, NetworkStats capacities and split_bound.capacity in the units report, as declared.
  • Ratios: delivery ratios, alpha, shares and caps, with no unit.
  • Routing costs: path costs, tunnel costs and their sums, which never take q. total_cost is cost × bandwidth units, so total_cost × q is cost × physical bandwidth.
  • Hardware money and power: capex and watts.

Counts are plain integers. An exact fraction is written {"numerator": n, "denominator": d}. A missing key and a null value differ: each field says when it is absent and when it is null. The analysis's outputs.details selects which detail fields appear (Output selection). T1 is a distributed_te model; T2 is a centralized_te model with a tunnel_count.

Placement totals and the run's metadata and units_report use the same field names in Python and JSON. In placement and capacity rows with a native result, that object and its plan, by_source and by_tunnel entries use the engine's field names. There a bandwidth amount drops _units and a drop count ends in _drops: delivered is delivered_units, source_drops is source_drop_units. Edges and nodes are ids (PreparedTopology.edge_refs names each edge), so edge_drops lists (edge, units) pairs, whose sum is edge_drop_units, and per-edge outputs are vectors in edge order; an unlimited request or design is infinite where JSON writes null with request_kind or design_kind "unlimited". For placement rows and capacity rows with a native result, kind is JSON only; a placement row's reference_shortfall_units (reference_request_units minus result.delivered) is also JSON only. A step's question is its typed query in Python, written in normalized form here (Results and export). Losses: Demands: how traffic enters; the worst failure case: Failures: patterns, cases and states.

Null when the sources are not weighted. weight_basis "capacity" | "explicit" | "residual_snapshot" or null What weighted splits are proportional to. Null when it does not apply to the model. edge_weights list of EdgeWeightJSON or null Explicit edge weights. Null when the model has none. tie_break "fewer_hops" | "higher_capacity" | "higher_available_capacity" | "higher_headroom" or null How equal-cost choices are ordered (ShortestPaths and T1). Null when the model is another one, or the WCMP controller programs the demand. multipath boolean or null ShortestPaths: whether every equal-cost walk is used (false: one canonical path). Null when the model is not ShortestPaths, or the WCMP controller programs the demand. parallel_edges boolean or null ShortestPaths and T1: whether every parallel link is used (false: one per node pair). Null when the model is neither, or the WCMP controller programs the demand. tunnel_count TunnelCountJSON or null The tunnel count per head. Null when the model has no tunnels. prefer_headroom boolean or null CentralizedTE: whether T2, after minimizing total tunnel cost, minimizes the plan's headroom penalty, based on occupied fractions of link capacity. Null when the model is not CentralizedTE. cost_ceiling CostCeilingJSON or null The tunnels' cost ceiling. Null when there is none. min_unreserved_bandwidth_units integer or null T1: a setup-search filter (integer units of q): a tunnel's search uses a link only when its unreserved capacity is at least both the tunnel's request and this minimum; nothing is kept free. Null when the model is not T1. route_names list of string or null The named routes of a pinned model. Null when the model is not pinned by named routes. controller "next_hop" | "group" | "all_routers" or null The WCMP controller scope that programs the demand. Null when no controller programs it. supplied_support boolean Whether a CentralizedTE model was given its own support DAG. supplied_program boolean Whether a pinned model was given a native program (its routes are not exported).

Null when the plan is T1's. headroom_penalty integer or null T2 with prefer_headroom: the headroom penalty of the plan. Null when the plan is T1's or prefer_headroom is off. max_lossless_offer_units integer or null T2: the program's lossless maximum offer F. Null when the plan is T1's.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text: Packaged JSON Schemas describe scenario inputs and exported results. They drive validation and IDE completion.

docs.title: Where the schemas are
docs.text: ngraph/schemas/scenario.json covers scenario inputs; ngraph/schemas/results.json covers the results file. Both ship in the installed package.

docs.title: What validation checks
docs.text:
The schema checks value types, required fields, allowed keys and simple constraints such as enumerations and minimums. Unknown input keys are refused with their location.

Scenario.from_yaml always validates against the schema before expansion. Rules the schema cannot express are checked in code: blueprint parameter names, risk-group references, and unrecognized keys in sections whose schema allows additional properties, such as workflow step parameters. Every refusal is a ValueError whose message starts with the field's path and value; a schema refusal keeps the schema's ValidationError as its cause.

docs.title: IDE Integration (VS Code)
docs.text:
Add to .vscode/settings.json (not committed to the repository):

{
  "yaml.schemas": {
    "./ngraph/schemas/scenario.json": [
      "scenarios/**/*.yaml",
      "scenarios/**/*.yml"
    ]
  }
}

The YAML extension then validates and completes scenario files as you type.

docs.title: Validate from Python
docs.text:
import json
import yaml
import jsonschema

# Load and validate
from importlib import resources as res

with res.files('ngraph.schemas').joinpath('scenario.json').open('r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)

with open('scenarios/square_mesh.yaml') as f:
    data = yaml.safe_load(f)

jsonschema.validate(data, schema)

docs.title: Top-level sections
docs.text: The top-level keys and what each holds are listed in Scenario YAML.

docs.title: For contributors
docs.text:
ngraph/schemas/results.json and the Results page are generated by dev/generate_results_schema.py from the result record declarations (plain records and their Annotated refinements) and the explicit fragments in dev/explicit_results_schema.json. Every result field has one description, where it is declared: the attribute docstring of a record field, or the description of a fragment node; the generator refuses a field without one.

ngraph/schemas/scenario.json is maintained by hand: update it whenever a top-level section, a field's type or a workflow step type changes. The Scenario YAML and Workflow Steps pages name every scenario.json property (a test checks it).

# Check every bundled scenario and integration YAML against the schema,
# and that the generated results schema matches its sources
make validate

docs.title: Workflow Steps
docs.text:
Scenario.from_yaml(text) parses an ordered workflow. Python callers execute run(prepare(scenario)); the returned RunResult.steps tuple holds each step's name, type, execution order, where its seed came from, normalized question and typed result. Duplicate names refuse before execution; step names longer than 100 characters are refused.

An unnamed YAML step receives <type>_<declaration index>. A step seed is explicit or derived from the scenario seed and effective step name (Seeds). Results are returned only after the complete workflow succeeds; ngraph run --keys exports selected steps after the whole workflow runs (Filtering Results by Step Names). The domain steps are separate from the analyses: BuildGraph provides physical NetworkX node-link data, NetworkStats describes topology, and CostPower (with the NetworkExplorer) presents hardware metrics. Built-in steps are immutable records (Records and editing); custom steps and result exporters: Custom steps and exporters.

docs.title: Keys common to analysis steps
docs.text:
Key Steps Default Meaning failure_policy MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement none A policy name from failures; each distinct drawn failure set is one case (Failures: patterns, cases and states) iterations MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement 1 The number of failure draws failure_trace MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement false Record the first draw that produced each failure pattern workers MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis auto auto or a positive number of worker threads seed every step derived The step's seed (Seeds) outputs MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis, MaximumSupportedDemand all off Optional outputs (Output selection)

Capacity and traffic-matrix placement resolve workers: auto to the CPU count; explicit positive worker counts override it, and results are the same for any number of workers. MaximumSupportedDemand (MSD) searches for the largest tested feasible alpha and runs serially (Maximum supported demand).

docs.title: BuildGraph
docs.text:
workflow:
  - type: BuildGraph
    name: topology
    add_reverse: true

Returns BuildGraphResult with node and edge counts (edge_count is two per link with reverse edges) and physical NetworkX node-link JSON. Reverse export edges are enabled by default. This operation exports the domain network, including disabled entities and their flags.

docs.title: NetworkStats
docs.text:
workflow:
  - type: NetworkStats
    name: stats
    include_disabled: false
    excluded_nodes: []
    excluded_links: []

Returns physical node/link counts and capacity, cost and degree statistics. The question records these effective filters. An excluded node or link name that the network does not have is refused at preparation.

docs.title: CostPower
docs.text:
Each level groups the nodes by the first parts of their /-separated names. A level deeper than the deepest node name repeats the rows of that deepest level.

workflow:
  - type: CostPower
    name: hardware
    include_disabled: false
    aggregation_level: 2

Returns hardware rows grouped by hierarchy level, with platform and link-end optics capex/power. The aggregation level is a nonnegative integer. The network explorer and inspect validate hardware too, and all of them read one hardware inventory: an optic counts only where its endpoint node has hardware, include_disabled: false keeps enabled nodes and links whose two end nodes are enabled, and invalid hardware (see the DSL components section) is refused in either view.

docs.title: MaxFlow
docs.text:
workflow:
  - type: MaxFlow
    name: ideal_capacity
    source: ^site1/leaf/
    target: ^site2/leaf/
    mode: combine
    preset: TE_MAXFLOW_UNLIM
    failure_policy: random_link
    iterations: 100
    workers: auto
    failure_trace: false
    outputs:
      min_cut: true
      cost_distribution: true
Key Default Meaning source, target required Selectors of the two node sets (Selecting nodes) mode combine combine asks one source-set/destination-set question; pairwise one per selector-group pair preset or model TE_MAXFLOW_UNLIM The model to ask (Presets; Routing models and admission); the two are exclusive offer, design_demand none Physical inputs whose applicability follows the declared model

The default question is unrestricted optimized lossless capacity. Choose SHORTEST_PATHS_ECMP, SHORTEST_PATHS_WCMP, SHORTEST_PATHS_MAXFLOW or an explicit model for another question. The result names the question asked (question) and where its offer came from (offer_source):

question When What it asks lossless_bound lossless admission and no offer The most the model delivers without loss fixed_offer_delivery an offer is given, or a lossy tunnelled centralized_te model has a design_demand What the model delivers of that offer (offer_source explicit or design) first_hop_experiment lossy shortest-path routing and no offer What arrives of an offer the Core derives from the sources' first hops

In pairwise mode a source group and a target group that are the same single node give a zero-valued self row; any other overlap of source and target groups is refused.

The result holds the cases in order, each with its rows under states.converged; each row holds the engine's result. Cuts, edge arrays and cost reports appear only when requested (Output selection; the kinds of cost report: Results and their units).

docs.title: TrafficMatrixPlacement
docs.text:
workflow:
  - type: TrafficMatrixPlacement
    name: traffic
    demand_set: peak
    alpha: 1
    failure_policy: random_link
    iterations: 100
    failure_states: [converged, stale]
    interaction: ordered
    workers: auto
    outputs: {cost_distribution: true}
Key Default Meaning demand_set required The demand set to place alpha, alpha_from_step alpha 1 The demand multiplier, or the MSD step that supplies it failure_states [converged] The failure states each case reports: converged, stale, repair interaction ordered ordered or simultaneous placement

Places the demand set, by default in priority order, then declaration order. Each row has a stable id, its endpoints, its reference request and the engine's result; each state adds totals, and the result adds each declaration's accounting of declared, resolved and discarded units. A failure changes which nodes and links can be used, never a declared volume (Failures: patterns, cases and states).

Each case reports the requested failure_states, each computed separately: converged computes the demands again on the failed network (declared group shares stay fixed caps, and dead caps are listed), stale forwards each baseline program unchanged and lossy, and repair re-splits the baseline programs over the surviving routes. A state whose bounded forwarding calculation cycles or reaches its round limit reports a forwarding failure with no rows. Group scope refuses converged and repair under a failure policy when it programs a router inside the IGP domain. The full rules: Failures: patterns, cases and states.

interaction: simultaneous forwards every demand at once, sharing losses on common links, as a lossy question on fixed programs; its rows are not comparable with the default ordered rows. A simultaneous step that takes its alpha from an MSD step cannot have pool demands. The full rules: Ordered and simultaneous placement.

Use either alpha or alpha_from_step, never both. Omitting both uses 1. alpha_from_step names an earlier MSD step and places at its largest tested feasible alpha. Preparation refuses a name that is not an earlier MSD step; the placement refuses, when it runs, an MSD result with no feasible alpha. The placement records the MSD step's name and the alpha it used (alpha_source, alpha).

docs.title: MaximumSupportedDemand
docs.text:
workflow:
  - type: MaximumSupportedDemand
    name: supported_load
    demand_set: peak
    alpha_start: 1
    growth_factor: 2
    alpha_min: 0.000001
    alpha_max: 1000000000
    alpha_tolerance: 0.01
    max_bracket_iters: 32
    max_bisect_iters: 32
  - type: TrafficMatrixPlacement
    name: tested_load
    demand_set: peak
    alpha_from_step: supported_load

Searches for the largest tested alpha at which the demand set is placed in full, keeping every probe (Maximum supported demand). alpha_start, growth_factor, alpha_min and alpha_max bound the search, alpha_tolerance ends it, and max_bracket_iters and max_bisect_iters cap its two phases; the example shows the defaults. alpha_feasible is null if no probe was feasible. search_status and stop_reason say how and why the search ended (each value: Maximum supported demand). MSD takes no failure input: the step refuses failure_policy, iterations and failure_states, and its probes place the set without failures. To place the alpha it finds under failures, give a later placement alpha_from_step and a failure_policy, as the Tutorial does.

When a demand set offers no traffic because all declared volumes are zero or every positive volume is discarded, MSD makes one probe at alpha_max. If that probe succeeds, it reports trivial, with proof and stop_reason both nothing_offered, and retains discard accounting. If scaling the discarded volume exceeds the native integer-unit range or binary64, the probe is refused and MSD reports range with stop_reason offer_range. A positive demand that merely rounds to zero is still searched as below_resolution.

An MSD probe is below_resolution if any resolved leaf of a positive declaration requests zero units after scaling and expansion, even when the declaration's rounded total is positive. It is never an accepted feasible probe or certificate endpoint; search moves upward from it. Before stopping on tolerance with no feasible probe and a below-resolution lower bracket end, MSD tests the first alpha where every such leaf receives at least one unit, found from rounding alone; an already tested endpoint is reused. It continues if feasible. If no feasible probe is found this way, it reports none_feasible with stop reason unit_resolution; iteration limits keep bracket_limit or bisect_limit.

docs.title: TunnelCountAnalysis
docs.text:
units: {resolution: 1}
network:
  nodes: {S: {}, a: {}, b: {}, T: {}}
  links:
    - {source: S, target: T, capacity: 1, cost: 1}
    - {source: S, target: T, capacity: 100, cost: 2}
    - {source: a, target: T, capacity: 2, cost: 1}
    - {source: b, target: T, capacity: 10, cost: 1}
demands:
  te:
    - {id: pooled, source: '^S$', target: '^T$', volume: 0, preset: TE_ECMP_16_LSP}
    - id: heads
      source: '^(a|b)$'
      target: '^T$'
      volume: 0
      model:
        routing: {type: centralized_te, source_allocation: equal, tunnel_count: {per_head: 1}}
        admission: lossless
workflow:
  - type: TunnelCountAnalysis
    name: counts
    demand_set: te
    counts: [2]
    up_to: 3
    design_demand: 2
    offer: 1000
    workers: auto
    outputs: {details: false}
Key Default Meaning demand_set required A set of tunnelled centralized_te demands counts none Distinct tunnel counts per head, each from 1 to 10000 up_to none The limit of the "up to" row design_demand, offer required The physical design and offer for every demand of the set

Evaluates every demand of the set once per listed tunnel count, then once "up to" the up_to limit, each row a fresh native evaluation of the demand's centralized-TE model with that count, lossy at offer and planned for design_demand. Every demand of the set uses the same design_demand and offer; the rows read no declared volume. The set must hold tunnelled centralized-TE demands only (centralized_te with a tunnel_count, or the TE_ECMP_16_LSP and TE_ECMP_UP_TO_256_LSP presets); any other model is refused at preparation. Self pairs and same-label group pairs do not create demands; empty selections and entirely excluded declarations have no tunnel-count rows.

Rows follow the set's demands, then the listed counts in order, then the up_to row. A row's count is the requested count per head (for the up_to row, its limit); the chosen count is plan.tunnels_per_head. The plan (fluid and whole-unit tunnel size, planned bandwidth, tunnel cost, headroom penalty, the largest lossless offer and insufficient_resolution) is written in every row; result holds what the offer delivers and loses. lossless_at_design_units is the lossless delivery at the design, min(design, largest lossless offer). Rows are not monotone in the count, and "up to" picks the smallest count that carries the live heads' design shares, not the count that delivers most of the offer.

The example fixes q to 1, which misses the default precision target for these amounts (Precision and the choice of q). In it, the pooled demand delivers 1 + 100 of its offer of 1000 with two tunnels (one per link) and its up-to row chooses one tunnel, on the wide link; the two heads deliver 2 + 10 with two tunnels each and choose one. A pool row's plan.total_tunnel_cost is on the analysis graph: its pool section's synthetic_ingress_cost of 1 is paid once per tunnel, which physical_tunnel_cost leaves out (3 and 2 here).

The step's offer is a known lossy offer for the TE ingress pools of its set, and it and the design take part in choosing the bandwidth unit q (Units and the resolution q; Tunnels and TE ingress pools). Naming the set makes it part of the run's prepared traffic like any step's set: its declared volumes and models still take part in choosing q and are validated at preparation.

docs.title: Output selection
docs.text:
outputs key Steps Adds to each row edge_flows MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis the units each directed link carries residual MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis each directed link's residual capacity after the row; under simultaneous placement, the one final residual every row shares edge_reservations MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis each directed link's tunnel holds saturated_boundary_edges MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis the saturated links at the sources' reachable boundary min_cut MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis the minimum cut closest to the sources, where defined (unrestricted optimized maximum flow); null otherwise cost_distribution MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement the cost report: delivered units per path cost, or the native marginal cost curve details MaxFlow, TrafficMatrixPlacement, TunnelCountAnalysis, MaximumSupportedDemand native per-source, per-tunnel, plan and call fields

All are false by default. Every row field is described in the Results reference.

Each output is selected on its own: outputs: {details: false, min_cut: true} gives compact rows with a cut, and outputs: {details: true} gives the detail fields without a cost report or cut. Omitted outputs, {} and details: false give compact rows; details accepts only a boolean. A row's pool is present either way, so a TE ingress pool's attachment cost stays identifiable. MaximumSupportedDemand accepts only details, which applies to its best rows; its probe history stays compact. Python spells the detail selector export_details (refused in YAML), and only Python can export every probe's rows (MSDQuery.export_probe_rows). details shapes only the JSON: Python results always hold the detail fields. Every other output exists only when requested, in Python as in JSON.

The results schema enforces each row's applicable detail fields: they are absent with details: false and present with details: true. A native result's plan is null when no tunnel plan applies; a tunnel-count row keeps plan at row level rather than inside result. Compact rows keep their drop totals: edge_drop_units sums losses on physical links and TE ingress pool attachments.
